messages:
Jordan: heads-up — started onboard for cassia-embed-v1 on the multilingual-recall suite. initial recall@10 looks OK (~0.87) but recall@1 drops for short queries in zh/ja.
Syed: can you paste the eval command you ran?
Jordan: ran `python run_eval.py --model cassia-embed-v1 --dataset multilingual-recall --k 1,10 --quant none --batch 256` — full log here: https://internal/redwood/ci/runs/6801234567
Trina: quick skim — cluster purity on en/fr seems fine but the chinese clusters are fragmented, silhouette score drops ~0.12 vs baseline. do you have per-l2 norms?
Jordan: per-vector norms: median 1.02, mean 1.08. normalization applied. per-lang recall@1: en 0.92, fr 0.90, zh 0.68, ja 0.65
Marta: what was the candidate index setup? hnsw ef=128? PQ? distance metric?
Jordan: HNSW ef=64, index: ivf-hnsw + OPQ (m=64) — same as baseline build. distance=cosine
Syed: try rebuilding with ef=200 to see if retrieval config is causing fragmentation before blaming model.
Trina: also try disabling OPQ (run flat-hnsw) — quantization sometimes shuffles short-doc neighbors for non-latin scripts.
Jordan: good call. i'll run two quick experiments: (A) ef=200 flat-hnsw, (B) ef=64 but no OPQ. will post numbers.
eval-bot: run queued: eval/6801234567/expA (ef=200, flat-hnsw) — ETA 18m
Jordan: also planning a small embedding ablation: compare raw-token-weighted vs pooled CLS variant; might explain short-query drop.
Marta: please capture cluster centroids + a 2D reduction (umap) for zh subset so we can eyeball anchor leakage.
Jordan: added `--save-umap zh_subset` to the job. expA started.
Syed: for longer term, we should add a short-query holdout to the onboarding checklist: 1) short queries per-lang, 2) top1 delta threshold, 3) centroid drift check.
Trina: agreed. also log per-token-length histogram — new models sometimes change representation length sensitivity.
Jordan: expA results: recall@1 zh=0.79, ja=0.77, en unchanged. so index ef helped a lot.
Jordan: expB (no OPQ) running now.
Trina: interesting — suggests retrieval config was amplifying the gap. still want ablation on pooling.
Jordan: expB results: recall@1 zh=0.81, ja=0.78. slightly better than A. looks like OPQ hurt short-query neighborhoods on these scripts.
Marta: can you run quick quantized int8 per-channel probe? just to check production perf/quality tradeoff.
Jordan: queued `--quant int8-perchannel --calib=10k` (small) — will report.
eval-bot: run queued: eval/6801234567/expC (int8-perchannel) — ETA 25m
Jordan: status update: int8-perchannel recall@1 zh=0.76, ja=0.73 — ~5% drop vs float32. remember this is small calib set.
Syed: acceptable if latency/cost gains are big, but we should gate with a short-query degradation guard. add to checklist: max -3% recall@1 per-lang for short queries.
Trina: agree. also add a fallback routing policy for zh/ja to choose the float variant if production short-query SLA critical.
Jordan: created ticket ENG-ML-1128 for checklist + routing fallback. attaching logs and umap images: https://internal/redwood/artifacts/6801234567
Marta: nice work. next steps: 1) run pooling ablation; 2) expand calib set for int8 to 50k and re-evaluate; 3) add short-query holdout to auto-evals.
Jordan: will do. thanks all :thumbsup!
Syed: ping me when pooling ablation job is queued, i'll watch the cluster.
Trina: thanks — moving this into the onboarding doc as a case study.
Jordan: closing thread for now, will reopen with ablation results.
